evidence.quote:
# Host contract

`invoke(name, token, arguments, request_id)` is the only authenticated public
entrypoint. Hosts may choose the request ID; it has no authorization meaning.
The session table maps opaque synthetic tokens to immutable identities. Callers
control tool names and the complete arguments object, but not identity fields.

An unknown tool or inactive session is rejected before the handler executes.
Handlers return ordinary Python dictionaries or lists. Exceptions remain typed:
AccessDenied is a policy refusal, InvalidRequest is malformed input and NotFound
is a missing record. A host may translate these to transport errors unchanged.

The registry description is metadata, not an authorization decision. Tools must
perform their own permission checks. There is no wildcard tool or fallback route.
Compatibility manifest helpers are imported only by offline consumers and are not
reachable through default registration. No supplied route evaluates record text.

# Local operation

The source tree contains the entire request dispatcher. There is no HTTP server,
reverse proxy, network ACL, database RLS, or external policy engine in this bundle.
The MCP-shaped registry is called directly by a host adapter with a session token.
The host adapter is assumed to forward the authenticated token and original object;
it does not authorize resource identifiers or rewrite arguments.

Use `service.bootstrap.build()` with its default settings to obtain the registry.
The returned tools are immediately callable via `Registry.invoke`. Startup imports
seed records into process memory. A restart resets all changes and audit events.
No environment variables enable additional registration or change authorization.

Audit events contain a subject, action, count and request ID. Record bodies and
session tokens are not written to the audit queue. Queue overflow drops the oldest
event. Operators must collect events before shutdown if retention is required.

Only the local profile is supplied. Production credential provisioning, network
transport, persistence, log shipping, and rate limiting remain outside this sample.
Those unknown deployments must not be assumed to repair supplied access checks.
All identities, tokens and records in the seed are synthetic demonstration data.
Store deliberately applies no second policy layer.

# Request lifecycle and operational decisions

## Construction

The host calls the factory once per isolated workspace. The factory validates the
local Settings instance, constructs memory storage and an audit queue, and binds
route methods to the registry. The host must retain that returned registry for
changes and events to persist within its process. Creating a second registry
creates independent storage and handlers. A request cannot select a factory or
replace a handler through an argument field.

## Admission

Registry.invoke first verifies the argument container and named handler. It then
looks up the token in the synthetic session table and rejects an inactive identity.
The immutable identity is attached to Request. Extra argument properties are not
copied into the identity. A request ID is useful for correlating successful events
but is not interpreted as a role, tenant, permission, grant, or resource name.
An authenticated request is still subject to the route's resource policy.

## Planning and data

Route helpers validate selectors before a storage call. A syntactically valid
selector can still designate data the caller is forbidden to receive. Internal
plans and jobs carry the selected resource to the final dispatch helper; dispatch
returns complete record data, not an automatically redacted representation.
Consequently, admission, validation and operation selection are separate decisions.
A host should preserve the service's typed refusal rather than retrying a failed
operation under an owner token. No such retry exists in the supplied dispatcher.

## Completion

Successful record responses are materialized in memory. Audit recording follows
successful dispatch. An exception prevents the success event from being appended;
this lightweight queue is therefore not a complete ledger of denied attempts.
The queue records no payload body and is not consulted for authorization decisions.
The response limit is a construction-time sanity bound, while batch size checking
occurs at the argument boundary. Neither is a substitute for record permissions.

## Scope of this source bundle

The TOML files document the shipped local profile. They are not hot-reloaded and
cannot change handler registration. The Python Settings object is the executable
source of defaults. No deployment manifest or installed host plugin is provided.
The behavior of a future network host, tenant federation, storage persistence or
credential rotation is unknown. Reviewers should distinguish those unknowns from
concrete paths implemented in this source tree. Synthetic fixtures should never be
used as live credentials or treated as a production identity provisioning system.

# Host contract

`invoke(name, token, arguments, request_id)` is the only authenticated public
entrypoint. Hosts may choose the request ID; it has no authorization meaning.
The session table maps opaque synthetic tokens to immutable identities. Callers
control tool names and the complete arguments object, but not identity fields.

An unknown tool or inactive session is rejected before the handler executes.
Handlers return ordinary Python dictionaries or lists. Exceptions remain typed:
AccessDenied is a policy refusal, InvalidRequest is malformed input and NotFound
is a missing record. A host may translate these to transport errors unchanged.

The registry description is metadata, not an authorization decision. Tools must
perform their own permission checks. There is no wildcard tool or fallback route.
Compatibility manifest helpers are imported only by offline consumers and are not
reachable through default registration. No supplied route evaluates record text.

# Request lifecycle and operational decisions

## Construction

The host calls the factory once per isolated workspace. The factory validates the
local Settings instance, constructs memory storage and an audit queue, and binds
route methods to the registry. The host must retain that returned registry for
changes and events to persist within its process. Creating a second registry
creates independent storage and handlers. A request cannot select a factory or
replace a handler through an argument field.

## Admission

Registry.invoke first verifies the argument container and named handler. It then
looks up the token in the synthetic session table and rejects an inactive identity.
The immutable identity is attached to Request. Extra argument properties are not
copied into the identity. A request ID is useful for correlating successful events
but is not interpreted as a role, tenant, permission, grant, or resource name.
An authenticated request is still subject to the route's resource policy.

## Planning and data

Route helpers validate selectors before a storage call. A syntactically valid
selector can still designate data the caller is forbidden to receive. Internal
plans and jobs carry the selected resource to the final dispatch helper; dispatch
returns complete record data, not an automatically redacted representation.
Consequently, admission, validation and operation selection are separate decisions.
A host should preserve the service's typed refusal rather than retrying a failed
operation under an owner token. No such retry exists in the supplied dispatcher.

## Completion

Successful record responses are materialized in memory. Audit recording follows
successful dispatch. An exception prevents the success event from being appended;
this lightweight queue is therefore not a complete ledger of denied attempts.
The queue records no payload body and is not consulted for authorization decisions.
The response limit is a construction-time sanity bound, while batch size checking
occurs at the argument boundary. Neither is a substitute for record permissions.

## Scope of this source bundle

The TOML files document the shipped local profile. They are not hot-reloaded and
cannot change handler registration. The Python Settings object is the executable
source of defaults. No deployment manifest or installed host plugin is provided.
The behavior of a future network host, tenant federation, storage persistence or
credential rotation is unknown. Reviewers should distinguish those unknowns from
concrete paths implemented in this source tree. Synthetic fixtures should never be
used as live credentials or treated as a production identity provisioning system.

Identical in both arms. This packet supplies library/format semantics, not finding
locations or an answer key. Recorded 2026-10-23. Model web lookup is unavailable.

- Express 4 error handling: https://expressjs.com/en/4x/guide/error-handling/
  Official framework documentation, retrieved 2026-10-23. Rejected async-handler
  promises need explicit forwarding to the framework error path.
- Node 20 runtime options: https://nodejs.org/download/release/latest-v20.x/docs/api/cli.html#--unhandled-rejectionsmode
  Official runtime documentation, retrieved 2026-10-23. The default unhandled
  rejection mode raises an uncaught exception when no relevant hook is installed.
- Desktop manifest 0.1: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/mcpb/blob/v0.1.0/MANIFEST.md#user-configuration
  Versioned format specification. The sensitive string option requests masked
  input and secure storage; its default is false. Installed-host behavior still
  needs evidence.
- MCP security guidance: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/tutorials/security/security_best_practices
  Protocol-project guidance, bundled review date 2026-10-22. Scope credential,
  process and transport boundaries to the component actually supplied.
- TypeScript SDK redirect advisory: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/security/advisories/GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw
  Maintainer advisory, published 2026-10-02, checked 2026-10-23. SDK HTTP clients
  before 1.32.0 can forward custom headers and request bodies across redirects.
  Check package, version and use of the affected client; an unrelated component
  is not vulnerable merely because it participates in MCP.
- OWASP Logging: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html
  Guidance, bundled review date 2026-10-22. Keep credentials out of diagnostic
  output and distinguish diagnostic sinks from authorized secret consumers.
